I have worked this land for many years, and I know what it can give us. This small plot is for growing food for my family—perhaps cassava or sweet potato—and I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer from the shops in Wete. We will use goat manure and compost from home to feed the soil, and I will plant the local cuttings we have always kept, not the new seeds from the government. My sons and I will tend this plot with our own hands; it is too small to hire workers, and Allah sends the rains so we do not need to irrigate.
